payload.purpose_context: Authors lose traceability silently today. finalize-tasks and map-requirements delete success-criteria and letter-suffixed requirement refs that authors wrote, a declared FR-006a can go unmapped without any failure, and coverage errors do not show which IDs the spec actually declared. This mission gives Spec Kitty one requirement-ID grammar, keeps authored refs intact, catches malformed IDs when the spec is handed to planning, and makes every rejection name its reason. Slice 5 toward 4.0.0rc5 under epic #1676; closes #2991, #3519 part 2 and the remaining scope of #2066.
payload.purpose_tldr: Make requirement IDs (FR/NFR/C/SC, letter-suffixed, cross-mission citations) parse the same way everywhere, stop finalize-tasks erasing authored refs, and explain every rejected ID.

payload.question: What status should SC-### success criteria have in the requirement graph?
Should letter-suffixed ids like FR-006a be supported?
How strict should the setup-plan requirement-id check be?
Include the qualified foreign-citation syntax (<mission-slug>#FR-013) in this slice?
Does the Intent Summary capture the mission correctly?
Once rejected refs are kept on disk, which rejection reasons fail finalize-tasks and runtime readiness?

payload.final_answer: Malformed + unknown fail; foreign_qualified never fails; a rejected ref never un-maps the WP's valid refs

payload.question: How is the setup-plan malformed-ID refusal carried through the orchestrator-api contract?

payload.final_answer: Reason in data: envelope keeps PLAN_SETUP_FAILED; payload carries typed reason SPEC_REQUIREMENT_IDS_INVALID; direct setup-plan JSON uses that code

payload.question: What do finalize-tasks and map-requirements write back for existing authored refs?

payload.final_answer: Never rewrite existing: finalize never rewrites an item; map-requirements writes added refs canonical, keeps existing byte-identical, dedups by canonical form

payload.question: Does the Engineering Alignment note capture the design correctly?

options: Yes: no accepted ref means missing
payload.question: Does a WP whose only requirement refs are qualified citations of another mission count as missing requirement refs (and so fail finalize/readiness)?

payload.final_answer: Yes: a WP with no accepted ref is missing and fails, even if it carries foreign citations. foreign_qualified itself never fails; the failure is the missing-refs rule (orchestrator ruling, auto mode, post-tasks squad finding R4)

payload.wp_title: Compatibility evidence: corpus scan and latency micro-benchmark
setup-plan requirement-ID check and orchestrator-api plan parity
finalize-tasks keeps authored refs, applies per-ref verdicts, reports parsed IDs
Runtime readiness uses the injected grammar and the shared verdicts
Requirement-ID grammar package and single-source gate
map-requirements accepts the grammar, is append-only, explains refusals
Consumer guidance: templates, prompts and checklist describe the grammar
ADR and glossary: record the single-grammar policy
